# OLYMPUS v0.0.23 build sheet (as written before the build, 2026-11-17, with §15 added after it)

> The round's build sheet kept whole as the contract the roles built to; **§15, as built, wins over any line above it that it contradicts.** DESIGN.md's log of 2026-11-19 carries the decisions. Where the code and a line below disagree, the code decides. The sheet's role ports and `.run/` paths are the build's scratch; the patches and handoffs are in `.run/v023/`.

# OLYMPUS v0.0.23, "The portrait is what you would see: the gun in his hands, the man as he stands, the rooms you have not seen, and the first hour through the door": the build sheet

Written 2026-11-17 for the round's five implementers (A, B, C, D, E) and the lead, who integrates. It is the contract between roles that build in parallel without talking. It sits on v0.0.22 as `.run/v022-design/sheet.md` plans it and `.run/v022/` shows it built (stage 0's `lead.md`, the roles' `a.md` to `d.md`, the lead's edits), with the v0.0.20 hunt's fixes (`.run/huntfix-v020/merged.md`) and the samples `held-devices` and `house-light` (`.run/samples-v022/`, shipped in v0.0.21) in; v0.0.22 sits on v0.0.21 (`.run/v021-design/sheet.md`, `.run/v021/fix.md`). Where a release as built differs from its sheet, the code decides and the role says so in its handoff. **This sheet supersedes `.run/v023-design/sheet.md`**: only that sheet's player-facing fixes carry on (FH-1 to FH-9, DC2, DC3), re-scoped by `carried.md`; its stage 0 (the mate refactor, `entryRule`), DC1, DC4 to DC7 and the three- and four-man stack wait (the stack for 0.5).

Where this sheet is silent, the docs decide: DESIGN.md and the user's rules first, then TECH §1.3, then the sections it cites, then the four lens notes it merges, each item naming its source: **P§n** (`.run/v023v-design/portraits.md`), **O-n** and **Mn** (`overhaul.md`), **FH-n**, **DC-n** (`carried.md`), **AW§n** (`anywhere.md`, its two look sets only), and two entries of DESIGN.md's log the lenses did not carry, **U** (2026-11-17, "we see what is in the rooms before entering them") and **DW** (2026-11-17, "i don't know what the "look behind the door" option does"). "As designed" means the mechanism, constants and tests in that note stand unless this sheet changes them. My own choices are marked (my call). Every conflict between the notes, and between them and v0.0.21's and v0.0.22's sheets, is settled in §0 and §4.

**Lines.** The portraits and overhaul lenses measured on v0.0.20; the carried lens on v0.0.22 as its four roles built it (tree 56a1fc65, without its integration's fixes, the hunt's patch or v0.0.21's fixer); this sheet was checked read-only on main's working tree (v0.0.21 being released). v0.0.21's release and v0.0.22's integration move every line. So **every hunk is named by its function**, and a line is only a pointer at main's working tree on 2026-11-17.

**Verified for this sheet** (2026-11-17, read-only on main's working tree; no worktree was made and nothing was run: every item below is from reading the code at the lines named):
- **Art reads no sim; render reads only the named sim helpers.** `tests/syntax.test.mjs` `MAY_IMPORT` (:227) lets `src/art` import core, data and art only, and `src/render` core, data, art and render, **plus** the pure sim modules of `SIM_FOR_VIEW` (:230: places/plan, light, sun, clocks, doors, people/perception, people/figure, time/alerts, arms/look, body/blood), which `view.js` imports directly (`import * as ARMS from '../sim/arms/look.js'`, `PERCEPTION`, `FIGURE`, `ALERTS`, `BLOOD`); main.js injects no reader into `createView` (:412, `{ stage, painter, uploads, cycle }`). `hitcard.js boardGear` (:132) says it outright: "standGear's, written here: art reads no sim module". So P§7's "`boardGear` reads `standSeen`" cannot be built as written (§0 item 14), and a new sim reader the view needs joins `SIM_FOR_VIEW` (§0 item 15; corrected by the check, §14).
- **`look.js` already imports the scenarios' looks** (`houseLook`, `handsOf`, `houseOf` from shoothouse.js, :96; `rangeLook`, :318, aggregates them and `opforLook`'s men). A seen record can read the role-players' frames and the stands' holds through `rangeLook` with no new seam (§0 item 16).
- **`opforLook`'s frames** (opfor.js:772) are 'stand', 'aim', 'run', 'crouch', 'cower', 'drop', 'hands', 'kneel' (hands up, knelt), 'sit', with `rifle.where` 'hands' | 'knees' | 'floor'; there is no 'fire' frame (a shot is the stage's flash over 'aim').
- **The card's two faults are in the code as P§1 says**: `hitcard.js FIG_ROWS` [4, 118] (:75); the flattening to `khaki`, `khakiShade`, `khakiInk` (:109, :249); `boardGear`'s guns `place: 'hand'` (:133), drawn by `doll.js rifleIn` (:585, :880); `gear.js RIFLE_PLACES` folds `lowReady`, `highReady`, `aimed` into 'ready' (:64); `standGear` (:153) and the note "'hand' is standGear's alone" (:45); `gearToFigure` (:165).
- **`target.js warm()`'s faces** (:216) are ten, without `['armoured', 'pistol']`: the user's own stand 2a on seed 4028068471 (P§1). **`liveGear`** (:58) empties a live man's hands for 'unseen'. `dress.js DOLL_LRU` is 24 (:17); `hitcard.js MAN_MASKS` keys a man's mask by his dressed doll (v0.0.21's item 15).
- **The dolls in main.js**: the loadout's preview (:682), the C card (:1321), the I card (:1342), each `dressedDoll(gear, …)`.
- **The four B goldens** are `ui-hitcard`'s ("B, the khaki board … golden digests", :180): belief, truth, mid and far.
- **The stage's people**: `render/memory.js recall` returns null for an actor it has never kept (:35, "draw it as it is"), and forgets everything on a new state (:32); the view's people loop calls it (view.js:884); the stands keep v0.0.12's rule (view.js:1064). `men.js` keeps a viewer's sightings of a live man on a saved `{ [key]: ms }` map (:19, `remember` :130: yours on `state.mind.contact.seenAt`), **but `forget()` (:134) deletes a man from it when he gives up** (a new man to take in), and the take-in's `contact.last` holds only the last window: the sim keeps no durable "ever seen" record (§0 item 34, corrected by the check).

**The release.** The user starred "Stack and clear" on 2026-11-17 and named the next thing: "will need to finish the visual overhaul that has already been discussed, and small note : the portrait of the NPC holding a gun does not display the gun they are holding, the portraits need to be more dynamic and show us what we would be seeing, including what they are holding" (with their ask of 2026-11-15: "the I and C menu preview of the character should show the currently worn gear ... when we start fighting real NPCs, they will have to be rendered in the target preview as we see them, meaning with their gear"). v0.0.23 is the overhaul's first round:

1. **The record (A)**: one reader of what you see of a person, `seenOf`, that every portrait draws from, read from the stage's own helpers (`gunLook`, `kitLook`, `rangeLook`), so the card and the stage agree at every tick; and the back of a man (`src/art/doll/back.js`), for a man turned away.
2. **The stage's knowledge (B)**: nobody drawn before you have seen him; a house you do not know drawn only as you see into it.
3. **The portraits (C)**: the gun in his hands on the card, where the stage paints it; the man as he stands (aimed at you, high, pistol aimed, kneeling, down, cowering, hands up, a device) and as he faces you (from behind when turned away, the head turned side on); you on the I and C cards as in a mirror, prone included.
4. **The carried fixes (D)**: the instructor's walk-in keys along #1's path, a room passed at the door taught as one, T naming the key it will not press, the goal line whole, Again's short brief, the menus in plain words, the drill's words, the live lane briefed as live, and the door rows saying what they do.
5. **The samples first (E)**: every look set this round and the next depend on, made and sent in the round's first days, with one "To score" page.

Before all five, **stage 0 (the lead)** lands what moves no tick: the three sets nobody has seen shot and sent, the pins and figures recorded, `again` threaded, two v0.0.22 saves, the anchors, the F numbers.

**Rules of the round:**
- Edit only your own files and named hunks (§1). Report any other edit needed, exactly, in your handoff.
- No commits, tags, pushes, releases or promotions. Never touch `.play/`, :8200, :8201, :8212, `../longhaul` or `../tradecraft`.
- Patches and handoffs in `.run/v023/` (unmerged patches survive a reboot there): `.run/v023/<role>.patch`, `.run/v023/<role>.md` (CHANGELOG bullets, doc text, figures before and after, every pin cell moved with the item that moved it, every edit outside your list, the stubs you tested against). Scratch under `/private/tmp/claude-501/olympus-build/v023/<role>/`.
- Worktrees: `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/v023-<role> v0.0.22` (or v0.0.20 with `.run/v023/stage0.patch` if v0.0.22 is untagged, as v0.0.22's lead did), `node_modules` linked from the main tree, then `git -C <wt> apply --binary .run/v023/stage0.patch`. Removed at the end (unlink `node_modules`, then `git worktree remove --force`).
- Five roles share the machine: A, B, C and D run the runner with `JOBS=2`, E with `JOBS=1` (its suites are small; its gallery runs one Chrome); only `QUICK=1` or a file with its separator (`'seen ›'`; `'portrait'` alone runs all ten portrait files, `'house-live'` every live file, `'ui-'` every browser file). While `lsof -nP -iTCP:8200 -sTCP:LISTEN` answers and the Mac has had input in the last 5 minutes, `JOBS=1` for everyone. Heavy suites wait for the lead's quiet run (§9).
- A quick file stays under `QUICK_FILE_CPU_S` 3 s × k of CPU; a case that would pass it moves to a heavy case of its own, "(heavy)" in its name, never into `QUICK_SLOW`.

**Ports:** A 8230, B 8231, C 8232, D 8233, E 8234, reviews 8235 and 8236, the lead 8239 (stage 0, the integration, the smoke, `OLYMPUS_TEST_PORT` for single browser suites; the runner claims 8240 to 8249 itself). 8237 and 8238 are left for designers. `tools/gallery.mjs` is run with `--port <yours>`, never its default 8212. Kill every server you start.

**Interfaces first.** Each role writes §3's exports as stubs with the shapes given, then fills them, and tests against its own stub of another role's export until that role merges. A's `seenOf` stub for C: `{ kind, gear: gearOf(…), hold: { how: 'rifle-low' | 'empty', right, left }, pose: 'stand', facing: 'front', aimAt: null, rangeM, read, key }` from today's readers.

**Integration.** As v0.0.22's: the stage-0 tree is the base, `B=$(cat .run/v023/base.tree)`; each role's patch is `git -C <wt> add -N . && git -C <wt> diff --binary $B > .run/v023/<role>.patch`, but C's, cut against the tree E1's merge left (A, B and E1 in: `.run/v023/after-ABE1.tree`), E2's against the tree C's left (`after-C.tree`), and D's against the tree E2's left (`after-E2.tree`). The lead applies them with `git apply --3way` in the merge order, running `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs`, `'house-pin ›'`, `'house-live-pin ›'` and `'seen-parity ›'` after each. Before its final run, each role rebases onto the integrated tree the roles before it left.

### The items, as built (the lens's mechanism stands but for what is said here)

1. **The gun on the card** (C; O-1, P§1, P§3.3). As designed, at the defaults G1 (the gun's pixels in the board's dark ink, `PORTRAIT_HOLD.ink` 0x2a2216, its lit pixels 0x3d3220), W1 (the painted man holds it where the stage paints it: the rifle across the body at the low ready, the pistol at the chest, `standGear`'s 'hand' place gone) and H1 (the hostage's hostile with his pistol at her head on the side away from her). The gun's and a device's pixels are drawn by `worn.js` into a part set of their own (`g.held`, as `g.quiet` marks the seams), so `paintHitcard` tones exactly those pixels, never the arms or the holster. `warm()`'s faces gain `armoured/pistol` (the one missing: the user's 2a), and every other (face, holds) the fill can give (`portrait-warm` finds them from 64 drawn seeds); `hostage/pistol` and `noshoot/phone` are there already, and there is no `threat/phone` (P§4's name: `engage.js seenFace` maps a phone to the 'noshoot' face; corrected by the check). A man in his own colours keeps the gun in its own colours.
2. **The card never contradicts the stage** (C; P rule 3.2.1). `liveGear` is retired: the card draws in a man's hands what the stage draws in them (V1), and the take-in's read stays in the words ("HANDS NOT SEEN · 2A"). Boards are unchanged in rule: their stage paints nothing in the hands until identified, so their card does not either. Together with item 6 the card never shows a man the stage has not shown you (§0 item 2).
3. **The record** (A; P§3.1). `seenOf(state, pid, { by, ms, mirror })` in `src/sim/people/seen.js`, as designed but for five changes: (a) the role-players' frames and the stands' holds come from `look.js rangeLook` (it already reads `opforLook` and `houseLook`), mapped by `FRAME_SEEN` (§3.1; my call), the carry from `gunLook`'s `carry` and `pistol.posture`, mapped by `CARRY_HOW` (§3.1; the check's call), never a new seam; (b) the hold, pose and facing names live in `src/data/portrait.js` (`HOLD_HOWS`, `POSES`, `FACINGS`, `FRAME_SEEN`, `CARRY_HOW`), read by the sim and the art alike, since art imports no sim (§0 item 14); (c) `light` and `cover` are not computed this round; `facing` is computed and **in the key** (the check brought F1 and F3 forward, §0 item 8); (d) `standSeen(face, holds, read)` is the board's record, called by target.js; (e) **the stage is not switched** (the check's call, §0 item 33): `view.js armsOf` keeps reading `gunLook` and `kitLook` as v0.0.22, because their records carry per-tick fields (`flash`, `kick`, `muzzle`, `aim`, `action.k`, `mag`, the pouches' counts) that a look memoised by `seen.key` would freeze; the record reads the same helpers, so "one quantity, one helper" holds through `gunLook`, and `seen-parity` (F85) holds the two to agree. `seenToLook` is not built; `gear.js gearToFigure` stays (it is `gear.test`'s oracle of the doll against the stage). A also draws **the back of a man** (`src/art/doll/back.js`, new: the back of the head or helmet, the carrier's back panel, a back-slung rifle whole, the hands hidden; drawn from today's doll's parts, read by C's `doll({ facing: 'back' })`), so C's L is not made larger by the facing.
4. **The man as he stands and faces you** (C; P§3.3; the facing brought forward by the check). 35. **The house's knowledge across a load** (item 7): the known cells are the view's and are rebuilt from the legs' states, a rule of the house; any other unfamiliar place (none this round) would need its own rule or a saved record (§10).
36. **The game already has a "To score" page** (the Esc menu's, `src/ui/cards/topick.js`, v0.0.20 item 10: the waiting sets tried live in play, runtime picks on `state.$look`, never saved), which the overhaul did not name. Settled (my call): one list, two doors. The gallery's index shows every open set (E); the Esc menu's page gains the rows this round judges moving, on the target card: "Card gun" G1 to G3, "Hands not read" V1 and V2, "Aimed" A1 and A2, "Pistol aimed" P1 and P2 (C's hunk: `topick.js ROWS`, `parseLook`'s keys, main.js applying `state.$look.card` to `PORTRAIT_PICKS` at the card's paint). ## 10. Risks (each owned)

- **C is the round's L** (C): four items, a pose engine, a renderer, a card's tones, the I and C cards, and the facing's wiring (A draws the back's parts, so C's art grows by prone and the side's head turn only). Order inside C: step 1 the gun (G1, W1, H1, the warm list, V1) on A's stub, shippable alone; step 2 the pose engine and the candidates' tables (cut for E); step 3 the record's hold and pose on the card, the I and C cards, prone, the loadout; step 4 the facing (A's back, F3's turn); the ship rules leave `PORTRAIT_POSES` false if step 3 is red and `PORTRAIT_FACING` false if step 4 is.
- **The stage is not switched** (A; the check): the record and the stage could drift apart if a reader changes under one only; F85's oracle reads the stage's helpers directly at every tick of 28 lanes, and F86 holds the stage's look keys.
- **"Bang" is starred** (C, the user): question 1's default (the check's) keeps its board's figure; the switch draws the gun there on your yes.
- **The poses are my design** (C): the defaults are the lens's; the sample is sent before C's merge, and a score in time is one table.
- **Unknown cells could hide what the drill needs** (B): the hall and the stack's own door are always in sight when the drill needs them; `ui-unknown` plays the drawn lane to the card; the bots read the sim, never the picture, so no bot can be blinded by it, which is also why a player could be (PLAYTESTS' entry plays a drawn lane by the keys before the user).
- **The rebuild at a load is a rule of the house** (B): any other unfamiliar place would need its own rule or a saved record; none this round.
- **People hidden in combat scenes only** (B): the base's crowd keeps PEOPLE's no-pop box; question 7 asks.
- **The walk-in key runs every lived tick below rung 2** (D): `house-tick-budget` and F60 before and after (under 0.1 ms expected).
- **v0.0.22's integration may rename what D reuses** (D, lead): stage 0 step 0 reads the tag; D follows the integrated names.
- **FH-10 can move ticks** (D): built only if they hold.
- **Two groups of samples wait on C's step 2** (E, C): if late past the third day, `mag-boots`' H moves to v0.0.24's stage 0; `portrait-pose` is sent as soon as it can be, since the poses ship on its defaults otherwise.
- **Five roles on one machine** (everyone): `JOBS=2` (E 1), `JOBS=1` while the user plays; heavy suites only on the lead's quiet run.

**Does v0.0.23 answer the note fully?** ("the portrait of the NPC holding a gun does not display the gun they are holding, the portraits need to be more dynamic and show us what we would be seeing, including what they are holding.") As written: the gun (items 1, 2) and the dynamic poses (item 4) yes; "what we would be seeing" only in part. "The view reads the sim only through readers main.js injects (`ARMS`, `PERCEPTION`)": false. `view.js` imports `look.js` and `perception.js` directly, allowed by `syntax`'s `SIM_FOR_VIEW` (:230); `createView` takes no readers (main.js :412).
